references.text: Here the mixed multitude (אסַפְסֻף) is mentioned, who left Egypt together with the Israelites—the same group that started the complaining in Numbers 11:4.
The Israelites complained in the same way in the wilderness and longed for the meat they had in Egypt.
The place was called Kibroth-hattaavah (graves of craving) because of the people's desire for meat.
The psalm describes how the people tempted God by demanding food according to their own desires.
The psalm refers to Israel's cravings in the wilderness and how they tempted God.
Paul uses the Israelites' cravings in the wilderness as a warning to believers not to desire evil things.
